content: Oseltamivir, marketed as TAMIFLU, is prescribed for the treatment of acute, uncomplicated influenza in patients who are 2 weeks of age or older, provided that they have been symptomatic for no more than 48 hours. TAMIFLU is also approved for the prevention of influenza in individuals aged 1 year and older. However, there are important limitations to its use that must be considered: The effectiveness of TAMIFLU has not been established in patients who begin treatment more than 48 hours after the onset of symptoms. TAMIFLU has no proven efficacy against illnesses caused by pathogens other than influenza virus types A and B. Influenza viruses are subject to genetic changes over time, and the emergence of resistance mutations may reduce the effectiveness of TAMIFLU. Additionally, other factors, such as changes in the virulence of the virus, may also impact the clinical benefits of antiviral medications. Healthcare providers should carefully evaluate current data on influenza virus susceptibility to antiviral drugs and the expected treatment outcomes when deciding whether to prescribe TAMIFLU.
